speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when your gait and limb ataxia first started and if it has been getting progressively worse? Also, have you noticed any other neurological symptoms like numbness, tingling, or difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any headaches, vision changes, or double vision alongside these balance issues? Has anyone mentioned that your speech sounds slurred or that you have trouble swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and recent natalizumab use, I'm concerned about a serious neurological complication. Have you experienced any recent flu-like illness, fever, or severe headaches before these coordination problems started? I will now request a brain MRI and a blood test for JC virus antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI. REQUEST TEST: JC_Virus_Antibody_Titer. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Brain MRI shows lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images reveal multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement. Vital signs are within normal ranges. Neurological examination confirms an ataxic gait, evidence of ataxia, and right upper limb weakness (4/5 strength). Note: JC Virus Antibody Titer results are not currently available in the provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings are highly suggestive of Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML), likely secondary to your natalizumab treatment for Crohn's disease. Although the JC virus titer is pending, the clinical presentation and characteristic demyelinating lesions are sufficient for me to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML).
